positions.as_written: Read the dial test as a test of this complex rather than of a single structure.
Expect lateral meniscal mobility to be the normal finding at arthroscopy.
Identify the tendon at arthroscopy before working in the lateral compartment, because it and the fascicles are the landmarks that orient the hiatus.
Protect the fascicles during lateral meniscal work.
Treat the complex as the rotational restraint of the lateral side and the collateral ligament as the coronal one.
Plan the femoral tunnels for this tendon and the collateral ligament together and in three dimensions.
Assess rotation at 30 and at 90 degrees before deciding what the complex has lost.
Preserve the fascicles where a repair allows it, because they carry meniscal position and nothing else does at the hiatus.
Avoid treating an isolated popliteus injury as a common finding.
